Handling an Existing Car Loan: Reaffirm, Redeem, or Surrender
What Happens to the Car You Already Have in Chapter 7
Debtors with an existing vehicle loan during Chapter 7 liquidation must choose between reaffirmation, redemption, or surrender under the Bankruptcy Code.
If you have a car loan when you file Chapter 7, the Bankruptcy Code gives you three choices for the car: reaffirm the loan, redeem the car, or surrender it.

Under 11 U.S.C. § 521(a)(6), if you do not either enter into a reaffirmation agreement or redeem the collateral within 45 days after the meeting of creditors, the automatic stay terminates under [11 U.S.C. § 362(h)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/11/362), and the lender can repossess the vehicle under applicable state law.

Under 11 U.S.C. § 521(a)(6), if you have not reaffirmed or redeemed within 45 days after the first meeting of creditors, the automatic stay ends for the car. The lender may then take whatever action nonbankruptcy law permits. Separately, [11 U.S.C. § 362(h)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/11/362) ends the stay if you miss the statement-of-intention deadline or do not carry out your stated intention on time.

If your monthly income less expenses is less than the scheduled payments, a legal presumption of undue hardship applies under 11 U.S.C. § 524(m)(1), though 11 U.S.C. § 524(m)(2) exempts credit union creditors from this presumption.

For 60 days after the agreement is filed, 11 U.S.C. § 524(m)(1) presumes undue hardship if your monthly income less your monthly expenses is less than the scheduled payments. Under § 524(m)(2), that presumption does not apply when the lender is a credit union.

If the vehicle is worth significantly less than the remaining balance, redemption eliminates negative equity, but paying in full at redemption requires immediate capital. Finally, choosing surrender relieves you of all personal liability on the note once the discharge enters, allowing the creditor to liquidate the vehicle without pursuing you for any remaining deficiency balance.

If the car is worth less than you owe, redemption lets you keep it for that lower amount. You need the full sum at the time of redemption. Surrender means you give the car back to the lender. Unlike reaffirmation, it does not leave you agreeing to remain liable on that loan after the discharge.
